records.benchmarkId: MAPLE independent same-indication randomized comparator and FOREST open-label persistence
records.benchmarkContext: MAPLE and SEQUOIA were separate blinded pivotal oHCM trials but had different comparators. FOREST long-term open-label follow-up is selected, not randomized durability confirmation.
records.observedResult: SEQUOIA NCT05186818 randomized placebo-adjusted peak VO2 +1.7 mL/kg/min at week 24. The independent MAPLE-HCM Phase 3 active-control trial found +2.3 mL/kg/min against metoprolol. FOREST-HCM observed in 296 oHCM trial completers median 51.6 weeks follow-up; at week 96 NYHA and KCCQ improved and LVOT gradient was reduced, supporting some on-treatment persistence.
records.uncertaintyReview: FOREST is not blinded and its parent-trial composition cannot be treated as SEQUOIA-only; cross-pivotal comparator differences prevent pooling and full subgroup interaction results are unavailable.
records.criticalRiskReview: Open-label responder selection and lack of independent long-term blinded replication limit strength of durability inference.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed research grade, independently positive direction for same indication and long-term observational persistence, but uncertainty remains.

records.benchmarkId: SEQUOIA randomized oHCM precedent, a different comparator and clinical trial
records.benchmarkContext: Both independent randomized trials concern symptomatic obstructive HCM and aficamten, but MAPLE was against metoprolol and SEQUOIA against placebo. Evidence supports replicated direction not identical effect or long-term MAPLE-specific durability.
records.observedResult: MAPLE NCT05767346 randomized 88 aficamten versus 87 metoprolol with 24-week adjusted peak VO2 difference +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1, P<0.001). The separate SEQUOIA trial reported a 24-week placebo-adjusted +1.7 mL/kg/min, 95% CI +1.0 to +2.4.
records.uncertaintyReview: Positive short-term direction replicated with different controls, but 52-week MAPLE treatment durability, all subgroup interaction CIs, and comparative long-term cardiac safety require more evidence.
records.criticalRiskReview: Effect may be comparator-dependent; no cross-study equivalence or direct comparison with another myosin inhibitor can be inferred.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 research grade for replicated direction with incomplete MAPLE-specific long-term durability and subgroup evidence.

records.benchmarkId: FDA multiple-endpoint error control and missing-data review standards
records.benchmarkContext: Both Phase 3 studies are distinct blinded placebo-controlled trials reporting highly significant prespecified primary UAS7 contrasts, but sponsor toplines omit full statistical analysis plans, confidence intervals and missing-data sensitivity results.
records.observedResult: EMBARQ-CSU1 at week 12 published a -20.2 UAS7 LS mean change at 150 mg versus placebo change -10.7 with P<0.00001 for the between-group comparison. Complete UAS7=0 response was 42.4% versus 9.3%, P<0.00001. Sponsor reported both dose regimens met primary and key secondary endpoints in this and companion Phase 3 trials.
records.uncertaintyReview: Treatment differences are supported by nominal tests and standard errors, but no full endpoint-by-endpoint multiplicity hierarchy, primary-effect confidence interval or missingness sensitivity was supplied in the released summary.
records.criticalRiskReview: Strong sponsor P values are not a complete blinded SAP, and randomized safety/completer data after week 24 remain incompletely disclosed.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 research assessment for strong reported statistical signals with material unreviewed missingness and multiplicity details.
